grammarPoints.subject: english
grammarPoints.title: Prepositions of place
grammarPoints.rule: Use prepositions like above, behind, in front of, between, next to, and under to describe where something is located.

intro_examples.text: The picture is above the fireplace.
intro_examples.jp: 絵は暖炉の上にあります。

intro_examples.text: The fireplace is under the picture.
intro_examples.jp: 暖炉は絵の下にあります。

intro_examples.text: The rug is next to the fireplace.
intro_examples.jp: ラグは暖炉の隣にあります。

intro_examples.text: The fireplace is between the bookcases.
intro_examples.jp: 暖炉は本棚の間にあります。

table.title: Prepositions of place

cells: The picture is above the fireplace.
The fireplace is under the picture.
The rug is next to the fireplace.
The fireplace is between the bookcases.
The armchair is in front of the fireplace.
The fireplace is behind the armchair.

notes: Prepositions of place tell you where something is located.
Some prepositions are one word (above, behind, under); others are longer phrases (in front of, next to).
The preposition comes right before the noun it describes: under the mirror, next to the stairs.

grammarPoints.subject: english
grammarPoints.title: Subject-pronoun agreement: it, they
grammarPoints.rule: Use 'it' to replace a singular noun and 'they' to replace a plural noun when answering where something is.
grammarPoints.pattern: Where is/are + noun...? It's/They're + preposition + place.

intro_examples.text: Where is the phone? It's in the kitchen.
intro_examples.jp: 電話はどこにありますか？台所にあります。

intro_examples.text: Where are the lamps? They're in the living room.
intro_examples.jp: ランプはどこにありますか？リビングルームにあります。

intro_examples.text: Where's the lamp? It's on the desk.
intro_examples.jp: ランプはどこにありますか？机の上にあります。

intro_examples.text: Where are the armchairs? They're next to the fireplace.
intro_examples.jp: アームチェアはどこにありますか？暖炉の隣にあります。

table.title: it vs. they

cells: Where is the phone? It's in the kitchen.
Where are the lamps? They're in the living room.
Where is the fireplace? It's between the armchairs.
Where are the shelves? They're above the fireplace.

notes: Use 'it' to replace one thing (a singular noun).
Use 'they' to replace more than one thing (a plural noun).
Contract 'it is' to 'it's' and 'they are' to 'they're.'
